𝔗₁.statement: Under the standing assumptions (a metric space $X$ with the `ProofData` bundle for parameters $a \in \mathbb{N}$, $q \in \mathbb{R}$, a complex-valued kernel $K$, integer-valued functions $\sigma_1,\sigma_2$ and sets $F, G \subseteq X$, and the tile structure on $X$ with the default parameters), for natural numbers $k, n, j$ and a tile $u \in \mathfrak{P}(X)$, $\mathfrak{T}_1(k,n,j,u)$ is a set of tiles. According to its docstring, it is the subset $\mathfrak{T}_1(u)$ of $\mathfrak{C}_1(k,n,j)$ given in (5.4.1), and in lemmas one assumes $u \in \mathfrak{U}_1(k,n,l)$.

ℭ₆.statement: Under the standing assumptions (a metric space $X$ with the `ProofData` bundle for parameters $a \in \mathbb{N}$, $q \in \mathbb{R}$, a complex-valued kernel $K$, integer-valued functions $\sigma_1,\sigma_2$ and sets $F, G \subseteq X$, and the tile structure on $X$ with the default parameters), for natural numbers $k, n, j$, $\mathfrak{C}_6(k,n,j)$ is a set of tiles. According to its docstring, it is the subset $\mathfrak{C}_6(k,n,j)$ of $\mathfrak{C}_5(k,n,j)$ given above (5.4.1).

URel.statement: Under the standing assumptions (a metric space $X$ with the `ProofData` bundle for parameters $a \in \mathbb{N}$, $q \in \mathbb{R}$, a complex-valued kernel $K$, integer-valued functions $\sigma_1,\sigma_2$ and sets $F, G \subseteq X$, and the tile structure on $X$ with the default parameters), for natural numbers $k, n, j$ and tiles $u, u' \in \mathfrak{P}(X)$, $\mathrm{URel}(k,n,j,u,u')$ is a proposition (a relation between $u$ and $u'$). According to its docstring, it is the relation $\sim$ defined below (5.4.2), and it is an equivalence relation on $\mathfrak{U}_2(k,n,j)$.

forest.statement: Under the standing assumptions (a metric space $X$ with the `ProofData` bundle for parameters $a \in \mathbb{N}$, $q \in \mathbb{R}$, a complex-valued kernel $K$, integer-valued functions $\sigma_1,\sigma_2$ and sets $F, G \subseteq X$, and the tile structure on $X$ with the default parameters), for natural numbers $k, n, j, l$, $\mathrm{forest}(k,n,j,l)$ is an $n$-forest on $X$ (an element of `Forest X n`). According to its docstring, it is the forest based on $\mathfrak{U}_4(k,n,j,l)$.
